I got into this game via a demo. The demo left me wanting more, and Steam had it on sale, so off I went to get it.

I'm on my second play through. The first play through was messed up beyond believe. I didn't know what was what and got stuck in a boss battle that I could not win. That bit frustrated me to no end and pissed me off greatly. I went off in search for a guide to overcome the boss battle. To my dismay, none of the guide helps as I've done something I should not have done: killing everything in sight and trying to spread the EXP love with all my party members. The end result was a severly gimped party lacking in both stats and skills.

I stopped playing for a couple of days and dived deep into the wiki. I learn the proper way to play the game, picked up a majority of the content that I just zipped past without realizing it, and focused on growing my party members the proper way. Second time around, the game was infinitely less infuriating and way more fun. The boss that I was stuck at in my first play through became a breeze, though the game did something rather nasty after that particular fight. Thank god I was somewhat prepared for it, equipped with both knowledge and power to overcome that nasty bit. The resulting satisfaction was very, very high. 

From then on, the game became something I want to explore in depth. I trawled through the wiki and its discussion pages to learn more about the mechanics of the game. Although I've been vigilant in keeping track of the missable content, there are still a number of things that I inadvertently got locked out of without realizing it. I am currently one boss fight away from the end of the game and already I am laying down the foundation for my new game plus. 

Despite the amazing depth of the game, or rather, due to it, the game will eat you alive if you don't know what you’re doing. The game does not make obvious certain crucial information from the get go. Playing the game with a lack of information can lead to a really bad experience, especially if you play this game the way you would a normal RPG.

With that said, the game is excellent for those wanting a good challenge. There is a vast amount of content within the game, and it should keep someone busy for the next 100-200 hours.

Update (22 Feb 2014): I've just finished my third playthrough and I'm taking a break to plan for my fourth playthrough. It seems that once you've finished the game once, you just keep going back for more. This game is one of my best investments in Steam.
Make this game exist again on Steam, or release the remaster for PC.  It's basically SAGA tactics.

I originally started this game on the 360 but never was able to finish it, partially because of the ridiculously skewed leveling system and partially due to a red ring of death. Despite my inability to get past a boss fight around 80 percent of the way through the game, I really enjoyed it, so I was glad to see this game on Steam. 

I was even more glad when I started to play TLR again and realized a couple of things: it's a lot easier if you understand the skewed leveling system (and I'll get to that in a second) and the PC version has made a lot of interesting quality of life improvements to the game. Really, it feels like the only thing missing from the PC version is... achievements. (Okay, actually, my other complaint would be that whomever did the cutscene animation has apparently never watched a living person walk before because the modeling is terrible but -- that's minor.)

So back to the leveling system. TLR is really interesting in that it removes all control from the player in terms of leveling characters and, to a certain extent, control over a character's actions in battle. So while the lack of control will take some getting used to I actually think the battle system is really fun, if unique. The leveling system, however, causes problems. Essentially TLR has two leveling stats: individual units/character stats (which the game auto-levels/assigns for you) and battle rank, which levels your entire party/army. What I didn't realize the first time I tried the game on the 360 was that having a high battle rank is... actually really bad. The higher the battle rank, the longer it takes for stat increases and the harder the enemies are to beat (to the point where if you have too high a rank, like I did, a boss battle literally becomes a one-shot and completely impossible encounter). So, I'm definitely having a much better play-through on the PC because (a) the PC version seems to have reduced some of the connection between battle rank and difficulty and (b) despite how counter-intuitive it is to NOT level in a RPG, I've managed to keep my battle rank pretty low. 

That said, the game has an interesting storyline (that I'm eager to finally finish) and is definitely a completionist's nightmare. The main questline is actually fairly short but there's a MILLION sidequests and a couple hundred challenge quests (e.g., kill a specific monter, find a particular item, gain a specific level, etc.) so there's a ton of stuff to do. 

If you have a good 40-50 hours to kill, you like the idea of transhumanism, and you like SquareEnix, or just JRPGs, I definitely recommend this one.

It's a very deep game, and unfortunately it requires you to plan ahead and optimize.  For your first playthrough go nuts, on the second playthrough look up some strategies :].

I hate it when people give reviews and they've only played a few hours, so I figured I should leave my opinion.

There's no grinding in this game, although there's a LOT of content for you to miss.  Don't be in a hurry on this one, but also don't try to be meticulous and look up everything on your first playthrough.  Enjoy the cheesy Rush cinematics!  And then familiarize yourself with everything you missed on the first playthrough and make your second one badass!

As a forewarning, some of the optional content is very difficult to access and conquer!  As far as doing the "100%" or "True Boss" you'll need to sink a lot of hours in.  That's a big reason I have so many more hours than most other reviewers.  I don't necessarily think that's a bad thing or that you're missing out on the awesomeness of the game if you don't find every rare boss monsters or the "True Boss".

Okay so as someone who I just checked has over 500 hours in this game...  I think that qualifies me to write a review on it.  

With that many hours I like the game.  I will break it down into the pros and cons for new players deciding.

Pros
Hands down my favorite large scale battle system.  It balances controling multiple squads facing off against armies without being to micromanaging and yet with still a bit of flexibilty.  Their are some frustrations and a steep learning curve to it though.  You rely upon the computer to bring up your selections and there is a lot of mechanics that go into it from your class, to your formation to your party leader.  Outside of combat selections and even your party build up can dramatically effect your combat.  But when you do finally get the hang of all that you can lead your forces into some truly epic looking and feeling battles.

Scenery is lovely in the game and has held up well.  Some areas get repetitive when you are still hunting for rare monsters but usually the areas themselves look pretty.

The leveling system i enjoy but it might not be for everyone.  Basically when you begin the game you get to decide how to equip your main character.  The rest of your party you can only choose one of three focuses so they are less customizable. But overall I like the fact that one game I can make him an assassin leading an army, the next a ninja and a combat hog, and a third game an epic healer magic user, and if you have enough patience you can master them all.

Negatives
The main character truly has an annoying voice and personality.  How can i play a game so much that I hate the main character?  Well because I truly love the epic battle system it is relaxing and a lot of fun and it gets better and more epic as you go through the game.  And the first time you pull of a synergy or you start busting out the remnants it truly does have an epic feel to it unlike many other games. So just suffer through the main character and enjoy the fights.

The storyline.. This game was built to have sequels.  It does not to the best of my knowledge have any in the works yet.  Would love to explore more of the world.  This one has a lot of potential.

The learning curve...  You will hate or love the game for the first few hours.  At about hour twenty your going to find someone trick in battle that you didnt realize you could do and things will be easier.  And then youll starting finding combos you can use for end game.  Or formations and specializations.  So the learning curve on this game sucks.  At a hundred hours your still going to learn new tricks and techniques to make the battles more interesting or fun.  Yet while it sucks to take forever to learn it means that there will always be a new little trick you can pick up that will help you later.  Or someone to add to your party in a combo you didnt think of.

So the grind is what will get most people though.  Doing all the side quests takes time.  And the first time you have to run across the great sand sea you will appreciate ground transportation that other games have.  This one you have your feet.  No way around it sorry.

Overall seems like there is a fair bit of negatives with the postives.  So why do I recommend it so highly?  Because like legend of dragoon the combat is interactive.  The effects in it have stood up the test of time and truly capture the chaos and epic feel of army combat.  Some games will capture that but this lets you control your army in a more fluid manner.  I wish other games had a similar UI. Basically even after 8 years since its release...  The game is still unique in its play and fun to engage in.  Hope some others will give it a try.  That they will be able to suffer through the learning curve and the challenges and find some enjoyment  in it.  And if enough like it hopefully they will make a sequel one day.

Thanks for your time and the short novel read.  Have fun my friends and best of luck to you.

If it's caught your eye, but you're on the fence about The Last Remnant, then you already love JRPGs; as such, I'll make your decision easy for you: Go hit Add to Cart, and kiss several hours goodbye.

As you could probably tell from the videos as well as other reviews, the core of The Last Remnant is a fairly traditional JRPG, though it has a pretty unconventional take on battle and party mechanics. In reality, your success in battle will *largely* depend on what strategies you embrace, and those decisions start well before the battle screen ever initiates. Your Party is made up of all the characters you've picked up or hired, which you then organize into battle groups called Unions. During a fight, each Union is given a set of pseudo-random commands, and you select one of those options for the Union to perform (see the third-from-last screenshot on the store page). 

While at first, this system feels like a complete roll of the dice, as you get a few battles under your belt and start developing your characters, there is actually quite a bit you can do to help create conditions that give you favorable battle commands. Moreso, there are actually a number of different schemes you can play with for Union organization. For sake of example, I've had equal success with having one healer in each of my Unions, as well as having a dedicated Union that serves as an all-around party heal/buff squad, backed up with a couple long-range attackers. In fact, range also plays a pretty important role in combat; units can be intercepted en-route to their intended target, granting a damage bonus to the intervening enemy squad.

Graphics are suprisingly top-notch for a game released back in '09. The spell and particle effects have aged well, and in a *shocking* twist, seem to have been ported favorably from the console version. The controls, however, didn't have as much attention paid to them. Check out warutaru's review for some crucially helpful steps in making the controls more PC-friendly!

All things considered, I have had an absolute blast playing TLR, especially for the mere ten bucks I dropped on it. I can honestly say it's one of the most pleasantly surprising games I've bought in a long, long time!

Many speak of The Last Remnant as being different.  True in a sense given the concept of unions however the game in a nutshell comes down to fight the most enemy unions at one time that is feasibly possible.  Exploration helps tremendously with progression.  The link system in which you select enemy unions is extremely addictive.

Surprisingly grinding is minimal.  The combat system is insanely well thought out.  Your union leaders matter as does protecting vulnerable unions.  Disengaging an enemy union at the wrong time can prove catastrophic.   The much spoken about BR or Battle Rank system in honestly nothing more than a gimmicky veil.  It's all about character progression.  I can go on for a 50 page essay but I'll just leave it here.

The FOV is terrible though editing a config file solves this problem quite nicely.  The game looks great for a 2009 production and runs in 4K super sampled.

Perhaps one day S/E will bring the remastered version to Steam and return this masterpiece to the worlds greatest digital gaming platform.

This game is for masochists. It probably has the most RNG out of any RPG I have ever played. Win? Lose? It is almost entirely up to the game to decide who wins or lose almost every battle.

That being said. I still love it. Although the game's RNG is so prevalent, there are also a ton of ways to slightly tip the scales in your favor (and boy do I mean very slightly). You choose the characters in each squad, the formation of the squads, the currently usable abilities of every character, making sure you have enough recovery items, manipulating characters into equiping stronger equipment, selecting how many "enemies" to pull into a single fight from the exploration view, ...

Yeah... this game is complex. Possibly the most complex RPG I have ever played, and that is saying something.

Another MAJOR topic before people get this game is the grinding and backtracking. You will be grinding, backtracking, and micromanaging a TON. But I always find it satisfying for some reason. You don't simply "level up." Instead your stats for each character are gradually granted at the end of each battle. Thus you have various stat ups on your characters pretty much every single battle. So you always get the sense that you are improving, even if it doesn't amount to most traditional leveling systems when you do the math.

Skipable Cutscenes!!!! Yay. Most RPG's do not contain skipable cutscenes (at least the RPG's I have played), and there are multiple bosses I had to fight ~10+ times. If I had to watch all the cutscenes again, it would have 100% been a dealbreaker. But so far I believe every cutscene is skipable.

Anywhere saving!!!! Yay. You can save your game pretty much anywhere in the game. No need to run back to a save circle. I often made save files after simply reorganizing my army in hopes that my new strategy would work better. There are lots of save slots (I think like 50 or something) so save away.

Also be prepared to google the shit out of this game. The game does absolutely nothing to teach you how equipment, items and customization work. There is no in-game beastary to find what enemy drops the item you need. There a lots of levels that require you to unlock successive areas via quests.

I really like how quests are handled in this game. You just do the quest on the spot. No saving up a giant list of things to do. No forgetting what part of a quest yo are on or who you need to talk to. Every quest is self contained.

Other topics:

Story? It's okay, but nothing amazing.

Voice acting? really hit or miss.

Sound/Music? surprisingly good. I love the world map theme especially.

Graphics? Really good. Tons of enemies and allies with great animations all around. However, the cutscenes are not up to pair with other Square Enix titles. But this game isn't really focused on the cutscenes.

Meh.... hopefully that is enough infor for you to judge if you want to give the game a try. If you are an RPG enthusiast this game is a must play due to how unique it is, and how incredibly complex the game is. I have currently played it for like 80 hours and I am still learning new things constantly.

I personally would not recommend this game because of it's "leveling" system. 
First all, I should note that I don't mind grinding and I hate JRPG's that have the moster's scale to your level, I hate being confined to how strong the developers think I should be at any given point in the game.
Needless to say this game has the enemies scale to your level but then goes a step farther to make it even worse with it it's "battle rank" (BR) system. The game increases the stats of enemies and decreases the xp received and the chance to increase one of your characters stats. This wouldn't be so bad but the BR sticks no matter who is in your group (or union or whatever they want to call it) so if you level up your main character and the first couple party members in the early part of the game then every party member you get later will be ridicilously weak with no real way to level them up to where they should be.
Honestly, google "the right way to level up" (skipping the fact a game shouldn't need an explanation of how to freaking level up) with The Last Remnant and they will all say to "avoid as many fights as possible". I do not want to play a game where the point of the game is to not play the game as much as possible.
This game is a masterpiece, and a hidden gem. Purchase it before they took the game out of Steam store on September 4, 2018.

I remember when I was a little too young to have a job. I played the demo of this game now and then, trying to figure out what it's all about, how to 'level up' in it, where to go... this game is truly unique and separates itself from any strategy RPG I have ever played. Square Enix hit on something really good with this game, and that is the idea of strategic army-like combat. You get party members of all kinds, from simple soldiers to guild mercenaries with special traits/powers and the generals of Athlum, who are undoubtedly some of the most powerful characters I have. These characters are organized in to "unions" which are groups of units on the battlefield. Improving your characters is done through what actions are taken the most by them, so if you have a character using mystic invocations a lot, he/she will improve in his/her mystic invocations (though you can certainly have them learn more than that, depending on the character). There's no real "leveling system", Battle Rank is more of a bounty-like rating based on how well you've done in battles (except that it doesn't decrease), and will affect how tough your enemies will be from there on out. It's mostly about having your characters use what you want them to get better at, and then utilizing those growing skills on the battlefield appropriately, which I really like to grow them!


Here's the catch that separates this from your typical Strategy RPG: They don't act singly. As I mentioned with the union system, they actually act as a group, so you select from 5-6(?) battle commands which vary based on many circumstances (you can see the wiki page for this game for more on that if you're curious, I highly recommend reading up on it before buying to make sure this game is something you'd want! Even try the demo!) You might get a command that says "Attack using Combat Arts" and "Attack using Mystic Arts". Selecting the first would have all units who possess a usable Combat Art use it, unless the AP cost is too high in which case they'll do a normal attack. The second would have all units who know a mystic art (not all units can be mystic users! Your main character, Rush, however, can learn all mystic arts throughout the story... I won't spoil how, that's what the wiki is for) use the one they know that doesn't go over the AP budget for that turn; Those without mystic arts would do a normal attack. Many factors influence what option shows up the most, or with the results you want, and it's these factors on the battlefield and in the character's training that make strategy all the more important. Organizing your unions appropriately, with formations that match the role you have in mind for them, and proper battlefield wit when the tide starts turning, make this game quite insane.


I highly recommend this game to anyone who is looking for something more... unique in the genre of Strategy RPG. First of all, I recommend reading the wiki, watching some Youtube videos, and playing the demo before you buy. This game isn't for the faint of heart, but it also isn't overly punishing (unless you just try to zerg everything without any forethought at all to your foe's strengths and your own weaknesses) I can safely say, that this is the most unique Strategy RPG I have played to date, on Steam and off Steam.

+ The one of a kind battle system will be either the biggest source of rage or fun in this game. In fact, whether you will like this game or not depends almost entirely on this system. 
There is significant hidden depth within the mechanics of battling but you are also cruelly punished for being oblivious, as the game doesn't bother to explain much more than the basics.

+ Story isn't too bad, albeit a bit plain. OST is swell which is saying something since you have to listen to the same tracks for quite a while. The music has a good variety though and they change up the battle tracks too.

+ Major improvement over X360 version as well as a significant difficulty step up. The polish balances the game a lot better.


- Enemy skill Overdrive is jaw droppingly OP. Your funeral. Their other killer skill Miracle will also make your jaw drop until you realise it wasn't half as bad as Overdrive.

- Quick time events are pretty boring but then you realise that deliberately missing some of them gives you some control over the action order... Still that's a pretty haphazard way to implement such a feature. Other chance based events such as activation of remnant arts are unreliable which can be a source of annoyance.

An amazing RPG. Full support. I am now playing it for my third time through and thought it time to give a review. Two pieces of helpful advice 1) Don't sell your stuff. Think of this game like FF9. If you don't collect the right items now you will miss out on content/spells/items later 2) Make sure your characters are specialized. Turn off your mages learned melee attacks, and turn off your melee's magic attacks. This will allow you to get the commands you want (they are randomized and pull from active abilities), and if you have toons with melee AND magic abilities then they won't get good at anything, but rather level 2 or 3 at everything (you WILL regret it later).

Great Characters & Story
Beautiful Visuals
Unique Battle System

It is one of the best JRPGs, if not the best.
Hope this will get a sequel one day.

Excellent Final Fantasy syle game with innovative and interesting combat mechanics and a surprisingly good epic storyline. Very high quality production values, nice graphics, decent sound and voiceovers. To those complaining that it is grindy or too hard I say turn on autosave and learn how to use unions and union formations - if you do this correctly you will find that the difficulty level is fine and that grind requirements are acceptable. It is not immediately clear that when you first go it alone you need to add any newly hired characters to your union formations before you fight - do so and enjoy.

Okay so having finished this game at a 100% completion with over 400 hours invested in it (I played it on X360 too, years ago) here's an actual non-biased review.

Pros:
The UNIQUE (and by unique I mean nothing compares to it in ANY game whatsoever) combat and leveling system.
Not only do you have to keep track of the classes (which, by the way, are in a very large amount), but you keep track of your stats (obviously), weapons, abilities (arts)...

Every weapon leads to different styles, different arts, different stats, different gameplay.. 

The customization possibilities are virtually endless. I really like the graphics of the various spells you cast, the combat is really fun to watch, and sometimes the game can get really, really hard (i.e. DLC bosses omg). But hey, I finished it at 100%, and I'm not some hardcore gamer. There's SO MUCH to learn about that when you realize how in-depth and complex the game mechanics are, it can get overwhelming and you might end up quitting. 

The wiki for it has a plethora of information, so you can't really "get lost". But there's so much to do that a 100% completion, played casually and just exploring without really being sure what to do... That's gonna take over 150 hours, most likely. 

NEW GAME +. oh yes, starting the game with large amounts of cash, and a few other things that I won't spoil.
The units and leaders: So. many. possibilities. You dislike a guy? Bench him forever. Want to make a party of only chicks? Go for it. Don't like the main toon? Don't play him. (But he can kinda do everything so worth using). 

Ah, also. Beautiful story, I really enjoyed the graphics (I mean I played it 7-8 years ago) and the universe you play in is quite large, there's a ton of quests to do. 



Cons? Sure there's a few. 
Kinda flawed, a little redundant sometimes, the main character is not the brightest guy..
Magic isn't as strong as you'd want it to be, sigh. S
ome bosses are super annoying and are tough to kill regardless of what you try. 
The items for your companions, well you can't really choose what they use. Some have unique items, and to properly "equip" them, you kinda have to learn how leveling works... which is very complex. Not complicated, complex.


Overall: for it's genre, a turn-based JRPG, I'm honestly giving it at 9/10. I don't see what could possibly make it have a bad score. The bad reviews are mainly because of people not taking the time to understand the in-depth mechanics. 
IT. IS. COMPLEX. But really, really, really fun.


TLDR: Very complex game. Unique leveling/combat mechanics. Endless customization. There isn't a lot of information in-game about how everything works (you need the wiki, srsly). But if you like RPGs, and turn-based rpgs, (enchanted arms, lost odyssey) you're gonna love this. It's freaking 13 bucks (to me at least) and has all the DLCs. Until Lost Odyssey gets to PC, I'll be playing this often.

If you like the "Final Fantasy" aesthetic, you'll surely like this. 

The Last Remnant has a very experimental combat system which is interesting if not a bit frustrating at times. The game is actually very difficult, and some boss encounters can take several hours to defeat. Make no mistake, this game is a grindfest. You will need to grind to progress through the game. Thankfully, the grinding isn't difficult, and I found it to be more tolerable than most games.

The game really shines durring the boss fights. If you are the right level, boss fights are super engaging, and will require strategy to defeat them for sure.
Just make sure you turn auto-save on before playing! If you don't, you may find a boss is too difficult and end up stuck with no way to return to the world and grind a bit.

$10 is a bit much, so I would recommend waiting for a sale, but I'm sure the more devoted fans of Square will find $10 a great deal for them.

If that sounds like your kind of game, go for it

I just realized that this game is no longer available on Steam since the PS4 remastered release. So I beat this for the second time as a refresher and just because I kinda miss playing it.

Talking about the mechanics, it's been more than a decade and I think it's still one of a kind. The idea of having classic turn-based JRPG mechanic that applies on unions rather than individuals still sounds a fresh idea IMO. The battle gets even more interesting when more unions are involved in a long battle, as it feels more like a war.

Though, there are still several shortcomings. At first, it feels like we should have more complex customization as we can have many units in party involved in the battle. However, turns out there are many limitations regarding the character development and the battle commands, that somehow feels a lot more simplified, even compared to the classic 4 units party turn-based game. That said, I still think it would be great to add more depth if there would be a sequel, as I said before that it already has an interesting core mechanics to begin with. But now that it's been years, maybe The Last Remnant will actually be the last after all.

I've heard a lot about people complaining the enemies were scaling to our Battle Rank that somewhat makes even small enemies felt difficult to kill. From what I experienced however, the difficulty scales with more factors than just BR. I feel that it also adapt to our story progression, and it also seems that each map has its own constant factor, like no matter how high my BR is, I know which area of the map that always have weakling enemies. And those are at least several factors that I know. So, people said "Grinding is pointless as it only makes the enemies get harder" is kinda misleading I think.

Moreover, I find that it's more of a fun challenge rather than something to complain about. For me personally, the difficulty of turn-based game is not defined by how often we should grind, but rather more about tactical decisions (with reasonable amount of grinding of course). I mean, I wouldn't complain that I have to play around with combat/mystic arts more often to kill small enemies, rather than mashing normal attacks to kill weaklings repetitively.

But enough of this review, you can't buy this game on Steam anyway...

First off, this game is AMAZING.

Let me start with the bad, just to get it out of the way.

--The animation can use some improvement BUT it does NOT effect how well your gameplay may be. In fact, it might even be seen as comic relief, esp. with how the units ragdoll when terminated in battle.
--The story could be executed WAY better; not to say that it's completely poor, but there are some cutscenes that are lacking in specific reactions and some relationship development that could've been included to bring about a far more emotional pull.
--They don't really give you too much information about the connections in the plot and the background.
--In my own personal opinion, it lacks a couple that probably would've been amazing if they made it canon.

Now, onto the AMAZING:

--AMAZING plot/story with AMAZING characters. They're all dorks, seriously. While relationship development and animation could've been better, they are all unique in their own right. Even the ones you can hire to be as a part of your own union have their own personalities, and some of them come with their own sidequest to get into. The plot itself could have been explained a bit better but it is DEFINITELY worthwhile with a type of ending that tends to be unique among games and even stories themselves.
--The bosses, while incredibly difficult and ragequit-worthy, are CHALLENGING. You really need to think and strategize how you sort out your unions and how you use each character and especially what moves you make. Each boss has their own style of being beaten, and it's really awesome to get into how exactly to defeat them. Their moves are unique to them, so you have to think of ways to get around it if you die repeatedly the first twenty times. It isn't easy, and THAT'S what makes it so fun. It can be considered near IMPOSSIBLE because one of the bosses you encounter in this game, The Gates of Hell, is just lkmifowmfoIAMOIAmf rage everywhere BUT I /thoroughly/ enjoyed each battle, no matter how hard I did rage.
--The OST is to DIE for. Every single piece is AMAZING.The battle themes? They REALLY get you pumped and it IS download worthy. And you remember that boss I just mentioned? The Gates of Hell? The music that plays during that fight is absolutely SPECTACULAR; it's one of the reasons why I didn't give up straight away.

The battle system seriously needs it own paragraphs because of how UNIQUE it is and how PERFECTLY it's set out.
--It's kind of like chess, except more elaborate and you operate in what they term 'unions'. The formation and the leader and the units in them are customizable; the unit limit allowed in battle as well as the number of unions is small atfirst but as you go through the game, it increases. The units themselves, unfortunately, are not customizable but the main character certainly is.
--The commands are tailored specifically to what abilities the leader has, and to an extent the rest of the union. They are also dependent on situation and the items in your inventory as well as where your unions are position on the battlefield, which makes it realistic.
--When you launch your commands, the sequence itself that plays out gets you on the edge of your seat and it's actually REALLY mesmerizing to watch. It's not boring at all and there's the option to get involved in helping your unions attack because there's a live trigger that appears sometimes (I tend to put it on automatic but if you like getting immersed in the game then there it is!).
--No character operates individually unless you specifically assign only one character to a single union (which is probably a straight ticket to them dying). Each character works together and it's REALLY charming, in my opinion, because you can really see their teamwork (especially when they're allowed consecutive turns due to the live triggers) buuuut I digress. What I'm trying to say is that this battle system isn't like any other, simply because the way you command them is not as individuals, but as a whole. This means that they attack as a whole, they heal as a whole, and they, well, /die/ as a whole. I'm not sure what other game exists out there that has kind of the same system (except maybe Warcraft and Dawn of War but they aren't exactly turn-based), but nothing else really comes to mind so The Last Remnant REALLY takes the cake on unique battle system.

I've probably just rambled really badly in this review but I REALLY REALLY REALLY recommend this game!! I'm actually REALLY surprised that it isn't popular because I would've thought that the story and gameplay would hook people in despite the downsides. All the same, this deserves a FAR bigger fanbase so I really encourage anyone that happens across this review to try it out. Just pleeeaaasee aahhhh. Not even this review can express how amazing I think this game is.

I absolutely love The Last Remnant. As someone who's played many, many (J)RPG since the early-90's, I can say that this is one of my absolute favourite JRPGs ever. The game got a bad reputation when it was released because it was filled with bugs, but they repaired them (fortunately): it now works perfectly well.

Also, one of the weakest point of the game is that, while they explain a lot of things at the start of the game, they don't explain the most important points to really "master" this battle system: if you don't try to gather some information on it, or if you don't analyse enough what you're doing after a while, you will probably get frustrated at some point. It is a nice JRPG, that tries to do something different with its battle system. But it is deeply flawed in the following ways:

1. Graphics optimisation is poor. Textures pop in a lot, which is annoying. Sure you can mess around with certain files to fix it, but most people won't want to bother doing that.

2. You really do need to force V-Sync outside of the game, otherwise expect some messy screen tearing.

3. The plot is generic enough, but it does the job. Where it sort of falls away is you could probably blow through it quite quickly. The real meat of the game seems to be over the other side, with side-quests. And there's a ton of them, lengthy ones, quick ones, and so on. A few of them get closed out reasonably early on in the game, so if you're a completionist, you'll be spending lots of hours getting through these at the expense of the main story.

3b. The main story progresses at lightning pace. Honestly, sometimes all you have to do is go to the main story location, watch some cutscenes for 20 minutes and then maybe have a boss fight, and repeat. (At time of writing I've got to the halfway point with 30 hours, about 28 of those hours were doing side-quests and travelling imho.)

4. Battle system is interesting but horrendously flawed and frustrating. Basically you create armies or battle groups of up to five people per unit. And they all share the same health pool and action points. You give them commands to attack certain enemy units. Usually you want to keep physical and magic users separate so they can all use either physical or magical attacks together as mix and matching doesn't always allow characters to act together. 

Also, you generally put a healer in the unit so they can heal when they get hurt. Here's a ridiculous example of a frustrating battle:

I fought a battle and ended up with 1 unit left vs 1 boss monster. They were far apart, so couldn't attack each other. My unit had just beaten everything else on the battlefield, but it had a mere 90 hp left out of thousands. That unit had several healers. The enemy unit was almost dead. All I needed to do was heal, and own it. But the game refused to show the heal command, instead my choices were close in to attack next round, or wait. So I waited three times. No dice. The game then took away the command to wait, and forced me to move in. I had lots of Action points, at least three of my characters in the unit knew how to heal in various ways. In the end, the game gave me one choice; Attack physically (or attack with physical skills). No heals. So I attacked, and I died.

Here's the kicker, when you die it is game over. So reload time, wait through cutscenes all over again and retry the bloody fight. All this could have been averted by healing, but the game stubbornly refused to allow me to do so. And this is exactly where it becomes so frustrating, here is another hour to be wasted fighting the same battle, a particular pain in the butt if it is a difficult one anyway!

5. Levelling is apparently a no-no

Every guide out there suggests avoiding to grind, as enemies scale somewhat and will just ruin your day. Although it's not as bad as people make out, it can add to the frustration.

This game is often criticized by its (Battle Rank System), in which you gain ranks by fighting enemies, but sooner or later lands in a situation where a certain monster/boss is just seemingly impossible to beat. That's because enemies scales with your Battle Rank, whenever you gain rank they do too (albeit at a way higher stat gain than yours). The problem with that is your later recruits will be under-ranked due to them not gaining rank IF they are not in your party. Their initial Battle Rank is fixed and they await your recruitment at different points of story progression. So if you over-grind your starting lineup, you will end up with the game breaking issue where your later recruits will be dying constantly compared to your starting lineup due to the gap in their stat differences.

The solution to that would be to not overdo it by grinding early/mid game where it results in the issue of your later recruits being under-ranked (or rather your earlier recruits being over-ranked by the time you meet later recruits). There's really no real reason to grind until you're at the late/end game UNLESS there's a material you desperately need for upgrading weapons (the materials needed for upgrading gets increasingly more difficult to obtain as they near the end of their respective upgrade trees). The drop rate from monsters/gathering points are notoriously bad and might require more than multiple tries to get what you want. Personally I would recommend grinding after getting all or most of the main recruits just so you can collect everyone's upgrade materials all at once.

[list]

[*]You can't control how tough the world is, but you can.
[*]You can't choose your class, but you can.
[*]You can't do all the quests, but you can.
[/list]

I am now going to write some things about a video game.

This video game is called "The Last Remnant." Like many Japanese RPGs, the MC is a young child (called Rush) who is  estranged from his parents, and naturally this is a key plot point and one of the driving forces behind the story. This is generic and loathsome and not something I enjoy. However, the detestable MC, who is probably named after his tendencies to act brashly and without thought (Very subtle, game.) is one of the few characters I found myself disliking. I rather quickly grew fond of David and his 4 generals, for instance, despite their lack of any given motive other than to serve their leader. In fact, David's motives are perhaps the most confusing of all. I found myself playing on to try and discover what they were.

However, along the way, I was swept away by my love for the combat. It's highly detailed and strategy based; you create squads of soldiers and have them perform commands as a group. It's an interesting style and quickly captured my attention. However, it quickly lost it again once I realised how grindy the game is. It's also needlessly complex for newer players, not teaching anything more than "Attack enemies! Heal allies! Win fights! Don't lose!" The character progression system is overly complex, and is never quite explained, to my knowledge. I've done a fair bit of research, and the gist of it is that the more a unit uses a specific type of command, the better it becomes with that type of command (e.g magic, physical attacks, healing spells) and will learn more powerful abilities of that type. However, managing the equipment of your allies is hopelessly complex and grindy and this is where the game falls down. It's painfully slow in the early to mid game, and that's about as far as I got before getting bored and giving up.

It pains me to say that I don't recommend the game. It's an interesting game with a fairly nice range of characters, and there is some kind of ridiculously complex yet... existing plot. It features magic, so you know it's good. But the monotony, repetitive battles and grindy nature make it far too slow to enjoy. And this is coming from a guy who loves a good grind.

This game is intriguing beyond belief- just a bizarre RPG experience but a solid and very good one.
I highly recommend it to anyone who's a fan of the genre and wants to try something a bit 'out there'.

[h1]I only recommend playing The Last Remnant if you're willing to use a guide and look up things on a [url=https://lastremnant.fandom.com/wiki/The_Last_Remnant_Wiki_-_The_Last_Remnant_Guide ]wiki[/url].[/h1]

The Last Remnant feels like is a typical JRPG [b]EXCEPT:[/b]

The combat system is unique where you command squads of units rather than individual units. For example, you can tell your squad to attack, buff/debuff, heal, defend, etc. Then, each unit in the squad will perform actions accordingly.

The leveling system is a hot mess if you don't know what you're doing. I've read guides and wikis and still don't know how it works exactly.
The Last and best of the great JRPG era. Loading up for the first time for a new save in a few years. Got GooseBumps. Here we go, adult responsibilities are fleeting. Last Remnant is forever.

One of the greatest unique rpgs I've ever played.
Although the story is slightly lacking, there's so much more that makes up for it.

Pros
-The combat system
Instead of controlling a party of 3-4 people, you control an army of up to 18 people, allowing for tactical fun.
-The score
This is easily one of, if not the best rpg soundtracks of all time, the combat music especially will get you extremely pumped for battle.
-Lots of guild tasks to do and stuff to unlock
-Multiple playstyles for the protagonist
-Amazing graphics for the time that still hold up today imo
-Greatly optimized with controller support
-Tons more content than the xbox 360 release

Meh
-The story
Not the best I've ever experienced, but I still enjoyed my time with it.

Cons
-Lots of grinding if you want to be strong enough to do all the sidequests
-Punished if you grind TOO much and raise your battle rank too high
-Difficulty spikes

All in all I'm proud to call this one of my favorite rpgs of all time.
If you're a Jrpg fan, the gameplay and music alone is reason enough for you to give this a shot.

The Last Remnant stands as an interesting game, even among fellow RPG games because of its interesting... combat and character progression systems.
What may seem to be taunting and perhaps nonsensical at first hides a wonderful tactical experience that actually discourages grinding and instead encourages the usage of strategy and party planning.

Other stuff worth mentioning includes the superb OST, from its varied city and landscape themes to several battle themes, it's one of the best OSTs I have ever heard and not many can touch it!

If you like spending time managing and planning characters, crafting your own challenges or just having battles where your strategy more than counts, The Last Remnant is my definite pick.

Of course, certain mods by certain someone will make this game even better while eliminating a key flaw too~

wildly underrated game. this suffered from being subject to the review of the final fantasy crowd. there is a lot to like here. i have probably close to 200 hours in it, i played it offline back in the day, and time logging was kind of buggy back then. i want to say i would love to see a proper remaster, but not by the people currently running and working at Square Enix. If you can find a key, and like things that color outside the lines and do not mind alittle jank, i highly recommend.

One of the most unique RPGs I've ever played.It's like playing with a bunch of friends,you can direct their actions,but they also have their own mind.However you can decrease the randomness of commands to minimal once you understand the mechanism.

I always enjoy Square Enix games, especially this one, I haven't finish the game yet, but I found it really enjoyable. The Last Remnant.

It's one of those rare games that compel you to keep on playing. A one of a kind JRPG created by Square Enix that focuses on skill based tactical combat rather than simple select action>hit enemy with playable characters as in the FF series. With several Hero characters & a lot of generic soldiers to choose from,each with their own styles & weapon sets,the amount of replayability is quite high while trying out the different teams & formations. Plus the ability to control the flow of battle by raising morale,inflicting status effects or simply bludgeoning through the enemies is an added bonus.  Plus there are guild tasks which can be completed to earn new formations,items,money & new certificates that unlock even more tasks & prizes.

One drawaback of the game is its tendency to get repetitive as it heavily depends on grinding to build up skills & find materials to upgrade weapons & accessories. Plus monster spawns.especially the rare kind are randomly generated & sometimes it gets extremely frustrating to get a monster spawn at a specific area to get it killed & unlock new items & magazines that helps in getting previously unavailable monster drops.

Overall,It's a great game to have for both RPG & JRPG fans as well as tactical gameplay lovers. The bosses are great & have a few hidden bosses(DLC) that are extremely tough to beat & requires careful planning & approach.

It's also one of those few games that I have played & possessed as a torrent download,a disc & finally a digital distribution.

My rating for the game will be a 8-8.5/10.

To put it simply: this is one very decent JRPG if not for the combat system, which although quite novel can be excruciating at times.

Story: meh. 
Nothing exciting happen and the plot goes far too slow to be enjoyed. Kinda funny for a  game titled The Last Remnant when most of the time the remnants only appear as uninteractable background objects. 

Characters: okayish somewhat
Most of your party characters are mercenaries who have no contribution at all to the main plot. Some of them are (awesome) unique characters with nice side quest tho. It's hard to beat a 4-armed catman armed with dual halberds.

Music: okayish somewhat
The battle theme is nice to get your blood boiling but it get repetitive after a thousands battles

Gameplay and Mechanic: revolutionary? Yup. Frustating? Hell yeah it is
At first you'll be presented by a bunch of combat mechanic (deadlock, flank, rear assault, etc) that sounds awesome on paper but hardly useful on real battle. Most mooks are weak enough to be killed from just a simple deadlock while enemies who truly need strategy to be downed HAVE a high deadlock threshold to even be flanked. 

This game also has one weird level scaling (kinda like TES IV: Oblivion) wherein your enemies level growth is high. The more you grind the more unkillable the enemies are until you can't do anything beside restarting the game. So, minimize your grind.

And the most frustating thing is the combat command. In this game, you can only give your squads vague ideas about what they're supposed to do next ("Use combat  arts!!!" "support them!!!" etc) and the ai will pick his action from his assorted abilities. The problem is it's fuken random, as in at critical time the command you need won't even appear.

Example: 
You need to heal without breaking the deadlock?  Nah, this time the game only giving you an option to break the deadlock, heal, get raidlocked by enemies, BAM your squad downed  

Let's use some strategy! Squad A to tank the damage while squad B attack from afar -> the command "Attack from  afar!!!" on squad B does not appear + the idle command does not appear  -> Your weak defense, high magic squad must fight the giant behemoth head on -> squad B downed.

Technical wise surprisingly (compared  to other SE jrpgs, at least. *cough *cough* FF XIII series) this game has a superb port. Nice graphic options (not just simply low, medium, and high), good translation, good keyboard support (mouse support is meh but you don't really need a mouse for this game), and most of all no random CTD.

Buy this game if you love JRPGs and can't stand not to play one. If you're not, only buy it when discounted.

A very intricate and interesting JRPG, if a bit frustrating at times.

The combat system is very unique, with some positive and negative quirks.
The world itself is gorgeous, once the textures load.
Characters can be a bit hit and miss but that's rather standard really.
Questing and crafting are both interesting to a point, if slightly repetitive at times.

More than worth the current price before it disappears on September 4th, hopefully to make room for a remaster.

I've played this game for numerous hours on Xbox 360 and loved it, starting over on PC is rough, but I like the graphics improvements.
I saw the PS4 and Switch remasters, but not enough changed to warrant another purchase.

I would like to see a complete remake or reboot of this game and allow it to continue in a series.

As you may already know, this game has an unique mechanic, its either hit or miss IMO. But I really love this game for this.

After over 100 hours and maybe 3-4 times restart halfway through the game (because I can't defeat one of the side mission boss, its almost impossible to beat unless you know the trick), now I can finally beat him for good. Its so fucking hard for godsake, I don't even remember how many times I decided to stop playing 'cause I'm not even sure if the bosses are beatable, but I just keep coming back to it. Got this game way back when it was released on the Xbox 360 and got this on Steam right before they stopped selling it. This game is highly underrated for how good it is and am surprised at the lack of reception I received given that it came from such a popular publisher (Square Enix). The game has its flaws, but it is really fun setting up you teams for battle and having a strategy for each team and how they will work together as a group and with the other teams. A 10/10 game that unfortunately didn't get the reception it deserved.

Square Enix did a great job on this turn-base RPG. It has a unique turn-base combat system that offers a diverse team building. Just a heads up, like many games of its era, it has poor dialogue in it's cutscenes. Wish this game had a longer story for more gameplay.

This is easily one of my favorite games. The story is absolutely terrible, but the world and the aesthetic of the world are both excellent. Where it really shines is the combat system. It's complex and a bit confusing, but incredibly good.

If you like a game with a huge cast of characters that you can actually utilize, if you like thinking about your team makeup and making hard decisions - tweaking and planning etc. this is a good game for you.

If you can forgive it's flaws, this game is quite unique and potentially very enjoyable. However, it has a ton of shortcomings. I'd give it maybe a 7/10. I'm only recommending the game because it's $10. If it were anymore, I don't think I could recommend it because there are just so many flaws.

You can't properly control what your units do. There are many mechanics in the game that are way too convoluted and not at all well enough explained or explained at all. The story is meh. The dialogue is meh. You can't run away from battles. Many mechanics don't make sense or are just plain wonky. You can't equip your units! You have to buy stuff and hope somebody asks to wear it. What if you bought something that cost 900 million gold and hours worth of crafting components and nobody asks to use it? Well you're shit out of luck. The crafting system is tedious and a joke wth a gazillion different parts. The same enemy models are reused over and over and they jump in difficulty like crazy for no apparent reason sometimes in adjacent zones even though they have identical models and names and are right near each other. You explore the same zones over and over for side quests. If you're trying to be a completionist and do all the side quests, it can take a long time and can at times feel tedious and grindy. For me, I wanted to try an all-female party run, but there are not enough female characters to recruit, most of the female characters are generics, and they all have bad stats compared to the unique male characters so you end up really gimped and a lot of bosses are like HP checks so if you don't have the required HP you get rekt. Thankfully this game has auto-save in the PC version though.

Some great, unique ideas in this game that just sadly weren't properly well done. The graphics are pretty good, especially for a 2009 game. A TLR 2 or a spiritual successor that takes this game's concepts but fixes its flaws would be amazing. Square Enix would never invest in such a gamble though I don't think. Especially not while they're just focusing on milking Final Fantasy series.

The Last Remnant is an excellent RPG and Strategy game. While it does focus on group combat, where you can't choose each individual's attacks, it does allow for a more realistic feel to combat. Enemies attack in groups, and use the same kind of tactics that you use. While the game has an "auto" save slot, do not expect it to use it. Save often, and be careful about where you go. Not all quest are simple, and bosses are a notch above other enemies. The story is interesting, but there are alot of cinematic scenes at a frequent rate.

Overall, it's worth buying. It's an interesting game, and I've enjoyed what I've seen so far.

I love me some jrpgs, but I haven't enjoyed one quite like this in some time.  The game is huge and there is plenty to do.  Setting up the parties and setting what works well is one of my favorite aspects.  If you like jrpgs give this a shot, you won't be disappointed.

There is a lot to like about this game.  I definitely recommend the game, but I wanted to give a warning to potential buyers.  This is one of those games where you can run into a brick wall of difficulty in several places.  Make sure you take your time, get all the generals you can get, spend the time to get the best gear, and learn all the different aspects of combat.  If you aren't use to tactical positioning, you will end up crushed in a few places.  If you aren't use to using statuses (negative and positive) you will get stuck.  If you rely too heavily on ultimate attacks, you will lose.  Take your time and learn the game well, or you will get very frustrated.

7.5/10  Fun, but you can get stuck very easily, leading to restarts.

Not a single game in the world has fighting mechanics like this game does. Someone needs to make either a sequel to this game, or use and improve on this kind of fighting system - feels more like a war instead of just 4 people against 20 enemies and they state it's an all out war.
Seriously, if you haven't played this game, do it! It will be a unique game that will never leave your mind.
OH, and F off stupid hell gate boss.

Love/hate relationship with this game, there are obviously some questionable mechanics that didn't get the praise from the players (for example the way you level stats and skills, the commands, the battle rank system itself), even worse, it isn't explained in the game.

But still it is very unique, sadly I have never seen a game like this, sometimes feels like a mini total war game but with JRPG mechanics, managing and fighting multiple units at the same time, it's sui generis.

What I can suggest for anyone starting this game is to use TLRPlanner and checking the wikia for more information that the game doesn't give itself, these two tools can, sometimes, be the difference between hating and loving this game.

This game is interesting and very unique. I am still conflicted about whether I really recommend it or not though. To be honest I have not finished the game yet, and am only writing the review now because I have stopped playing the game for now. There are many things to love and hate, and to be fair I recognize that this is a game that was made on a game engine that was brand new to the development team at SE. To put it briefly, for everything I liked about this game, there was a part of that feature that drove me nuts.

So here's the deal, things to love about this game include the diverse and culturally rich world with lots of different characters that are all pretty cool. The graphics are awesome (as expected from an Unreal engine game). The story is captivating and enjoyable. There is plenty to do in this game. The battle system is a must see and is almost worth buying just to experience it because it is so unique, or at least it is not like anything I have ever seen before.

Now, things that will get on your nerves... (unfortunately it is often easier to say more about the negative, but that doesn't mean the game is more negative than positive)

While the world is amazing there not as much revealed about it as I wanted. You see many different races of characters and they all live together apparently peacefully, but why? They have diversity, but don't really use it very much in the story. The characters could have all been human and it would have made little difference. Their attributes in battle are not even that different.

The story is great, but admittedly hard to follow (not a surprise from a JRPG really). It was easy to get lost because there is not always indication of where to go to advance the story. Side quests offer some fun side stories, but can be terribly confusing even when using a guide.

The graphics look awesome, but the non-movie animations are awkward. Even some of the movies have parts where the voice acting do not line up with the expressions and movements (translation problem, maybe?)

The battle system is very impressive in concept, but nigh impossible to figure out. After 60+ hours of gameplay I still don't know what I am doing. Simply stated, it is a convuluted mess that is overcomplicated and chaotic. There are so many variables and things to adjust that I was just overloaded and gave up trying to figure it out. Even forums of experienced players can't make a lot of sense out of it. It seems most players ignore the majority of it and for good reason. You can recruit from a huge assortment of characters, use over a dozen different formations, assign leaders, occasionally be given the choice to have them focus on magic or combat, all of it makes little sense though and possibly little difference. It is essentially information overload in an attempt to give the player the choice to devise their own strategy. Speaking of strategy though, actual battle gives you little control at all. You simply give a general command and the characters choose which moves to use themselves. This can be super frustrating because what you want to do is sometimes not an option. Also, there are so many different variables in battle that you could fight the same battle twice using the same commands, and you might lose terribly the first time and win by a landslide the next. So much for all the strategy... I used a stat grinding trick for about 6 hours from a guide I found online and my characters grew incredibly, but still I have battles that just end badly. Luckily there is an autosave feature on PC, but you must turn it on first. It is off by default.

The character progression makes little sense. You know battling monsters makes you stronger and it would appear the stronger the monster, the greater the growth. Things like exp points are absent or invisible. Stats are shown on character views, but no indication of how far along the progress is or how to increase it. Each character also has a unique stat that no one knows what it actually does. There is a Battle Rank which would appear to be synonymous with Level in other RPGs, but it is not really explained what it means. Guides actually show that Battle Rank is better the lower it is because the battles get harder the higher it is. Monsters are stronger the higher your Rank is, which happens to be a feature of some RPGs that I absolutely despise because it makes all the time battling and grinding completely unsatisfying. Final Fantasy 8 works similarly, so if you have played that you might be familiar with it. As the story progresses you increase the number of characters you can use in battle, but you don't reach the max until late in the game, so your characters will end up heavily imbalanced because only characters you use will grow.

Sometimes what I like most about JRPGs is the soundtrack. I will say this game's is a rather generic fantasy one though. It is ok, but nothing to write home about. Certainly not one I would listen to outside the game. I actually find myself playing on mute though, listening to my own music or watching a show while I grind. 

All in all, I give it a 3 out of 5. I stopped playing because I lost interest and after reading a ton of guides and forums I decided it is so unnecessarily complicated that I don't care to figure it out. I just want to see the rest of the story and have it be over. I guess I will recommend it because if you haven't played anything like it before, it is an interesting experience. I bought mine in a Final Fantasy bundle, so if you can find it in one of those for cheap, it is worth buying.

Pros: 
-The squad mechanics and large scale battles are unique and done well enough to make it feel like you are leading an entire platoon into battle instead of 3 or 4 party members.
-lots of things to hunt, grind, craft, and solve.
-the graphics were really bad for the first bit until I found some tips online to improve the quality. The game can look decent enough. Not quite final fantasy good (even for it's time).

Cons:
- the story. All of it. None of it makes a lick of sense. Spoilers ahead: your sister is kidnapped, you set out (before the game even starts) to find her. You somehow mistake a middle aged silverhaired woman for your 12 year old bruenette sister. She takes you to the local King who decided to offer his complete support to the local village idiot (you) for no reason whatsoever. Then you get side tracked. Then a conquerer invades. In a sense a huge amount of random events happen that are so loosely tied together as to only be understood by men in tinfoil hats. Dark souls has an easier story to follow.
-narrative. It is extremely hard to follow anything going on. Several times you are told to go to a city for an event. You go there and nothing happens. You try to leave and people get mad. The quests are boring, long, and all amount to marching to objective killing everything in the path.  The main story has no objective list to follow so unless you pay absolute attention to the cutscenes you will have no idea where to go.
Characters- the main character is a complete idiot, and not the fun kind but the moron who makes everything take too long. The support characters are stereotypes to the max. Even the villians are stereotypical (either meglomaniac crazy guy, or quiet all powerful type). 
Stats- most characters have a 4th stat that is mysterious or useless. Stats like love, gluttony, management, and others are found somewhat randomly and their effects are rumors at best. The Game doesn't tell you anything about them which is odd for how much hand holding it does with everything else.
Level design- some dungeons are blissfully short, some (looking at you great sand dessert) are so big that you never even reach the edges of. The short ones are at least finished but the big ones are just...empty. there nothing but a few big monsters. And it's those big levels you end up hating because you know, you just know, that some stupid side quest is going to make you march across it half a dozen times.
-last thing, cutscenes animations. When ever anyone walks during a cutscenes, it looks like they motion captured a string puppet instead of a person. No one walks right, no one moves their arms right if at all (looking at you torgal, with your semi permanent folded lower arms), and no one generally moves in an appealing way.

In short the game has some genuinely neat features that the rest of the game completely overshadows worth poor narrative, poor story, bad cast of characters, and terrible movement animation.

I have beat the game and put in over 100 hours of active playing (I have a padded time in steam because of leaving the game on while doing other things) so I think I can give this a fair assessment.

This was a bit of a let-down.

The rich world and combat system had amazing potential, which fell woefully short on execution.

Lets start with the world; you are given this great mystery of the remnants and trying to find an answer to their existence, but we are given a short and terrible story to progress through the game with. Towns and surrounding areas are all but-nonexistant because of the way they designed the maps to be enclosed and small. We are given a protagonist who is an utter idiot, and we are supposed to believe all these hyper-competent leaders want to follow this stupid kid who does nothing but mess up and make stupid on-the-fly decisions? The antagonist had potential. in the first disc whenever he shows up he is a pure badass, but then he keeps showing up randomly and leaves randomly. They were stretching it, it seems they just wanted him to do something badass and then disappear again, even though him being at that place and his subsequent actions make no sense. The voice acting is far below par, they have decent VAs but it seems the direction they were given was poor. 

The worst of it is the character animations during conversations and cutscenes. I read they had motion capture work done, and it seems ALL of it went into the combat animations which were amazing, but cutscene and conversation animations are so bad it is jarring, and it took me right out of what was happening. This is saying something, I have a high tolerance for mediocre character animation, this game crossed a line somewhere.

Now the combat... Oh the combat, how you had the potential to be a JRPG game changer. "Lets take something tactical and add randomness and take away most of the player control, that would be brilliant!" No SquareEnix, no, stop it, stop... it... stop it. Side tangent; has noone in this world heard of ranged weapons? Are bows and crossbows too complex of an idea, do they have to cast most of their magic in melee range? The combat system of unions and leaders was an amazing idea, but once you get to the actual combat, it becomes garbage. I have 60+ AP to spend, why are all the actions available under 16? The best you can do is remove options you dont want showing up to increase the chance of getting something good, which doesn't work enough to not be very frustrating. 

All of your unions will want to bunch up when fighting enemies, only way to stop this is to make them stay back. But as I said, there is a distinct lack of ranged options. Most of the magic in this game does NOT have a ranged option, not even healing. The magic that DOES have a ranged option will greatly limit what that union can do that turn, and the best magic is ALL melee range. Worst of all, you can not then control your union positioning, you can spread out these tightly packed unions all attacking the same thing, which leaves rare monsters and bosses with wide area AoE attacks to really really really suck.

So lets talk about what I did actually like about the game, the things that kept me interested enough to keep playing so long -- All the side things in the game. Hunting down rare monsters, getting my party members stronger, finding new unique leaders, toying with formations and union composition (especially for the really difficult opponents.)

The main quest line might suck, but all the side things to do in this game are what provide content worth experiencing. I absolutely love the SaGa system of character progression, no more grinding out levels to overpower your opponent, you have to be smarter about how you approach bosses. This can be exploited of course, no leveling system is perfect, but for your first play through, you are unlikely to manipulate the system. There is another downside - where SaGa frontier games allow you to build a suitable party early, the unique leaders in Last Remnant are spread out. So, leaders you get early will be a lot stronger than ones you get later, they did not scale recruits to your Battle Rank (your level as it were) they merely gave them starting stats which they think is sufficient for that point in the game.

Hunting down rare monsters and crafting materials... at points frustrating, very frustrating, but that just makes the pay off of getting them all the sweeter. Could have been handled better, sometimes the RNG really kicks you in the mouth.

I can not honestly recommend this game, what it does well, others do it better so you are better off with those. I was strangely compelled to keep playing to the end, but too much was not enjoyable. I will not be coming back to this game at a later time like the vast majority of my other games, I will not feel like playing this game again, it will collect dust in my steam library. Best I can say is that I really got my money's worth, as I bought it during a steam sale.

Real shame that this game will no longer on Steam. I play this game for 200+ hours but never finish it, not because of the game, it just that I sometimes do everything the game offer (I do all sidequest, hunt all rares, unlock all unique general, craft some high-end weapons for Rush and his crew, do all Arcanas, beat all superbosses, clear Ancient Ruins and beat all DLC bosses) and just save at final save point and leave it there for no reason. It is really a great game with really huge potential in its gameplay and its world even with mediocre, slow, and pretty uninteresting/cliche story, music also some of the better one in my JRPGs experience too.

The Good:
+ Gameplay, if you understand its extremely deep, complex, and confusing system that almost necessary to use Wiki. It is very fun both in battle and army building. The party building in PC version is the most fun thing for me, this game party is can include up to 18 people! which can be divided up to 5 group (called Union), and like many team-based games, you need basic role for your party like Physical Damage Dealer Union, Field Clearing Magic Union (with Special Arts or Arcanas), Healing Union, Tanking Union, etc. but you still can be creative and create the party that suit your playstyle, some people even did some challenge like all males/females, all yamas, all qsitis, only generic soldier, etc. The battle in this game is like a full-scale war, not just a battle, some story event is really epic with you guest Union alongside and enemies sometimes called backup, it really makes the battle feel so epic.
+ Its world and its lore have is really interesting but doesn't really explain clearly, you have to pay attention to all tidbits to understand.
+ Music is really good, I like it, especially various battle theme.

I have yet to finish the game but I'm currently at the last quarter of the game:

The world of The Last Remnant is interesting with different species inhabiting it, giving me a feeling like embarking on a journey into the world like I have never seen before. The story on the other hand is generic story you can find from almost every JRPG with characters that feel mostly copy pasted in from other games, with few exceptions. Still, the story isn't actually bad, just dull, and the characters rarely come out as annoying.

Main difference to your average JRPG experience is the battle system. Instead of micromanaging every single member of your team in turn based battle where you can see the order in which each of the character will act, The Last Remnant places you in charge of units of several characters, whom you give more broader commands of either attacking, healing or some variation between these two and the characters act accordingly from there. After the initial shock the battle system turns out to be surprisingly easy to learn. Sounds like nice idea for step away from all the micromanagement you usually encounter in these games.

Unfortunately, once the encounters get little harder, the battle system wets itself. The actions available for characters seem to be randomized so if you end up losing and fighting the same boss twice, the available attacks will change, making learning and readjusting your plan almost impossible. If several of your units are in need of healing at the same time, commanding your unit to heal is turns into game of dice and too many times you will find your team members topping those who have taken only few hits while ignoring those that are at the brink of dying. Luck plays some part in almost every RPG I have ever played by adjusting how effective your actions are (dice rolls for damage or who attacks first etc) but rarely have I encountered a game where its a dice roll whether your team of heroes decide to do what you want or not. I have fought encounters that I have lost within two rounds and won within four turns right after my initial loss without changing my tactics and I can credit this to nothing else but luck that has way too great influence for the combat than it should.

Overall, at its best The Last Remnant is enjoyable, although generic JRPG. At its worst it is unfair duel where you lose your fight not because of a bad decision or unsuitable tactics but because suddenly the game decides that you have to bring knife to a duel with guns, and your second might stab you into eye with it instead of giving it to you when the duel starts.

You could enjoy this game, but there are way better games out there so why not play those instead.
